nodes.summary: Let $\delta$ be the divide-and-conquer D-node count. Let $k$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $0 < r < 2^k$, put $n = 2^k + r$, and let $\nu_2(r)$ be the position of the lowest nonzero binary digit of $r$, counted from $0$ (the exponent of the largest power of $2$ dividing $r$). Then $\delta(n) = \frac{\delta(n-1) + \delta(n+1)}{2} + 1 - \nu_2(r)$.
nodes.title: Midpoint identity for the divide-and-conquer D-node count

nodes.summary: Let $\delta$ be the divide-and-conquer D-node count. For every integer $n > 0$, let $k = \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$, let $\lambda_i(n)$ be the level-$i$ D-node count, and let $n_i$ be the binary digit of $n$ at $2^i$. Then
nodes.title: Level-sum formula for the divide-and-conquer D-node count

nodes.summary: Let $\delta$ be the divide-and-conquer D-node count and let $s_1(m)$ be the number of ones in the binary expansion of $m$. For every integer $n > 0$, let $k = \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$ and let $n_j$ be the binary digit of $n$ at $2^j$. Then
nodes.title: Binary-digit formula for the divide-and-conquer D-node count

nodes.summary: The divide-and-conquer D-node count $\delta$ satisfies $\delta(1) = 0$.
nodes.title: The divide-and-conquer D-node count at one leaf

nodes.summary: The divide-and-conquer D-node count $\delta$ satisfies $\delta(2) = 0$, $\delta(3) = 1$, $\delta(4) = 0$, $\delta(5) = 2$, $\delta(6) = 2$ and $\delta(7) = 2$.
nodes.title: Small values of the divide-and-conquer D-node count

nodes.summary: Let $\delta$ be the divide-and-conquer D-node count and $s_1(n)$ the number of ones in the binary expansion of $n$. For every even integer $n > 0$, $\delta(n+1) = \delta(n) + \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor - 2 s_1(n) + 2$.
nodes.title: Successor formula for the D-node count at even arguments

nodes.summary: Let $\delta$ be the divide-and-conquer D-node count and $s_1(n)$ the number of ones in the binary expansion of $n$. For every odd natural number $n$, $\delta(n+1) = \delta(n) + \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor - 2 s_1(n) + 2$.
nodes.title: Successor formula for the D-node count at odd arguments

nodes.summary: Let $\delta$ be the divide-and-conquer D-node count and $s_1(n)$ the number of ones in the binary expansion of $n$. For every integer $n > 0$, $\delta(n+1) = \delta(n) + \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor - 2 s_1(n) + 2$.
nodes.title: Successor formula for the divide-and-conquer D-node count

nodes.summary: For every integer $m > 0$, the divide-and-conquer D-node count $\delta$ satisfies $\delta(2m+1) = \delta(m) + \delta(m+1) + 1$.
nodes.title: Odd-argument recurrence for the divide-and-conquer D-node count

nodes.summary: For every integer $m > 0$, the divide-and-conquer D-node count $\delta$ satisfies $\delta(2m) = 2\delta(m)$.
nodes.title: Doubling recurrence for the divide-and-conquer D-node count

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $r$ with $r \le 2^k$, $\delta(2^{k+1} - r) = \delta(2^k + r)$, where $\delta(n)$ denotes the number of D-nodes in the divide-and-conquer tree on $n$ leaves.
nodes.title: Symmetry of the D-node counts

nodes.summary: The number $\delta(n)$ of D-nodes in the divide-and-conquer tree on $n$ leaves (OEIS A296062) is defined by the recurrence the paper quotes from Coronado et al.: $\delta(1) = 0$, and for every natural number $m \ge 1$, $\delta(2m) = 2\,\delta(m)$ and $\delta(2m+1) = \delta(m) + \delta(m+1) + 1$. The value at $0$ is the junk value $\delta(0) = 0$.
nodes.title: Number of D-nodes of the divide-and-conquer tree

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $i$ be natural numbers such that the binary digit $n_i$ of $n$ (the coefficient of $2^i$ in the binary expansion of $n$) equals $1$. Then the level count of D-nodes is $\lambda_i(n) = 2^i - (n \bmod 2^i)$.
nodes.title: Level count of D-nodes when the binary digit is one

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $i$ be natural numbers such that the binary digit $n_i$ of $n$ (the coefficient of $2^i$ in the binary expansion of $n$) equals $0$. Then the level count of D-nodes is $\lambda_i(n) = n \bmod 2^i$.
nodes.title: Level count of D-nodes when the binary digit is zero

nodes.summary: Let $k$, $r$ and $i$ be natural numbers with $r$ odd, $r < 2^k$ and $0 < i < k$, and let $n = 2^k + r$. Then the level counts of D-nodes satisfy $\lambda_i(n) - \lambda_i(n-1) = 1$ if the binary digit $n_i$ of $n$ is $0$, and $\lambda_i(n) - \lambda_i(n-1) = -1$ if $n_i = 1$.
nodes.title: Level counts of D-nodes at consecutive integers

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the level count of D-nodes on level $0$ is $\lambda_0(n) = n \bmod 2$.
nodes.title: Level count of D-nodes on level zero

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $i$, let $n_i$ be the binary digit of $n$ at position $i$ (the coefficient of $2^i$ in the binary expansion of $n$). The level count $\lambda_i(n)$ is $n \bmod 2^i$ if $n_i = 0$, and $2^i - (n \bmod 2^i)$ if $n_i = 1$.
nodes.title: Level counts of D-nodes

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $k$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $r < 2^k$ and $n = 2^k + r$, and let $x$ be a rational number with $n = 2^k (1 + x)$. Then $x = r / 2^k$ and $1 + x = n / 2^k$.
nodes.title: Normalized form of $n = 2^k + r$

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n > 0$, the sum $s_1(n)$ of the binary digits of $n$ satisfies $s_1(n) = (\delta(n) - \delta(n+1) + \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor)/2 + 1$ in $\mathbb{Q}$, where $\delta(m)$ denotes the number of D-nodes in the divide-and-conquer tree on $m$ leaves.
nodes.title: Binary digit sum from consecutive D-node counts

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $r < 2^k$, let $n = 2^k + r$, and let $s_1(n)$ be the sum of the binary digits of $n$. Writing $\tau(m, k - 1)$ for the Takagi value of the dyadic presentation $m / 2^k$, one has $s_1(n) = 2^{k-1} \bigl(\tau(r, k - 1) - \tau(r + 1, k - 1)\bigr) + (k + 2)/2$.
nodes.title: Binary digit sum from consecutive Takagi values

nodes.summary: For a natural number $m$, write $s_1(m)$ for the sum of the binary digits of $m$ (the number of ones in its binary expansion). If $n$ is an odd natural number, then $s_1(n - 1) = s_1(n) - 1$.
nodes.title: Hamming weight of the predecessor of an odd number

nodes.summary: For a natural number $m$, write $s_1(m)$ for the sum of the binary digits of $m$ (the number of ones in its binary expansion). If $n$ is an even natural number (including $n = 0$), then $s_1(n + 1) = s_1(n) + 1$.
nodes.title: Hamming weight of the successor of an even number

nodes.summary: For a natural number $m$, write $s_1(m)$ for the sum of the binary digits of $m$ (the number of ones in its binary expansion). For all natural numbers $k$ and $r$ with $r < 2^k$, $s_1(2^k + r) = s_1(r) + 1$.
nodes.title: Adding a larger power of two raises the Hamming weight by one

nodes.summary: For a natural number $m$, write $s_1(m)$ for the sum of the binary digits of $m$ (the number of ones in its binary expansion). Let $k$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $r$ odd and $2r < 2^k$, that is, $r < 2^{k-1}$. Then $s_1(2^k - r) = 1 + k - s_1(r)$.
nodes.title: Hamming weight of a power of two minus an odd number

nodes.summary: A full binary tree whose root has left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ is a divide-and-conquer tree if and only if the numbers of leaves of $L$ and $R$ differ by at most $1$ and both $L$ and $R$ are divide-and-conquer trees.
nodes.title: The divide-and-conquer condition at the root

nodes.summary: A divide-and-conquer tree is a full binary tree in which, at every interior node, the numbers of leaves of the two subtrees differ by at most $1$. In particular a single leaf is a divide-and-conquer tree.
nodes.title: Divide-and-conquer trees

nodes.summary: For a natural number $m$, write $s_1(m)$ for the sum of the binary digits of $m$ and $S_1(m) = \sum_{i=0}^{m-1} s_1(i)$. Let $k$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $r < 2^k$, and put $n = 2^k + r$ and $x = r / 2^k$. Write $\tau(x)$ for the Takagi value of the dyadic presentation $r / 2^k$, and $\delta(n)$ for the number of $D$-nodes of the divide-and-conquer tree on $n$ leaves, given by $\delta(1) = 0$,…
nodes.title: Cumulative binary digit sums via the Takagi function

nodes.summary: For a natural number $m$, write $s_1(m)$ for the sum of the binary digits of $m$ and $S_1(m) = \sum_{i=0}^{m-1} s_1(i)$. Let $k$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $r < 2^k$, and put $n = 2^k + r$ and $x = r / 2^k$. Write $\tau(x)$ for the Takagi value of the dyadic presentation $r / 2^k$. Then
nodes.title: Trollope's formula via the Takagi function

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $i$, the binary digit $n_i$ of $n$ equals $1$ if $i \ge 0$ and the coefficient of $2^i$ in the binary expansion of $n$ is $1$, and equals $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Formula for the binary digits

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $i < 0$, the binary digit $n_i$ of $n$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Binary digits at negative positions vanish

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and an integer $i$, the binary digit $n_i \in \{0, 1\}$ of $n$ is the coefficient of $2^i$ in the binary expansion of $n$ when $i \ge 0$, and $n_i = 0$ when $i < 0$.
nodes.title: Binary digits of a natural number

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $r \le 2^k$. Write $\tau(r / 2^k)$ for the Takagi value of the dyadic presentation $r / 2^k$, and $\delta(n)$ for the number of $D$-nodes of the divide-and-conquer tree on $n$ leaves, given by $\delta(1) = 0$, $\delta(2m) = 2 \delta(m)$ and $\delta(2m + 1) = \delta(m) + \delta(m + 1) + 1$ for $m \ge 1$. Then $\tau(r / 2^k) = \delta(2^k + r) / 2^k$.
nodes.title: The Takagi function at dyadic rationals counts D-nodes (Coronado et al.)

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $1 \le r < 2^k$. For a natural number $m$, write $\tau(m / 2^k)$ for the Takagi value of the dyadic presentation $m / 2^k$, and let $\rho_1$ be the $2$-adic valuation of $r$, the position (counted from $0$) of the lowest nonzero binary digit of $r$. Then $\tau(r / 2^k) = (\tau((r - 1) / 2^k) + \tau((r + 1) / 2^k))/2 + (1 - \rho_1)/2^k$.
nodes.title: Midpoint recurrence for the Takagi function at dyadic rationals

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $r < 2^k$ and put $n = 2^k + r$. Write $\tau(r, k-1)$ for the Takagi value of the dyadic presentation $r/2^k$, write $n_i = \lfloor n/2^i \rfloor \bmod 2$ for the binary digit of $n$ at position $i$, and let $\lambda_i(n)$ be the level-$i$ $D$-node count, which equals $n \bmod 2^i$ if $n_i = 0$ and $2^i - (n \bmod 2^i)$ if $n_i = 1$. Then
nodes.title: Takagi values at dyadic rationals from level $D$-node counts

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $r < 2^k$ and put $n = 2^k + r$. Write $\tau(r, k-1)$ for the Takagi value of the dyadic presentation $r/2^k$, write $n_j = \lfloor n/2^j \rfloor \bmod 2$ for the binary digit of $n$ at position $j$, and write $s_1(m)$ for the number of ones in the binary expansion of $m$. Then
nodes.title: Takagi values at dyadic rationals from binary digits

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $r < 2^k$ and put $n = 2^k + r$. Write $\tau(m, k-1)$ for the Takagi value of the dyadic presentation $m/2^k$, and $s_1(n)$ for the number of ones in the binary expansion of $n$. Then $\tau(r+1, k-1) = \tau(r, k-1) + (k - 2 s_1(n) + 2)/2^k$.
nodes.title: Consecutive Takagi values at dyadic rationals

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $k$, the Takagi coefficient $\ell_1(n, k)$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The first Takagi coefficient vanishes

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, every integer $k$ and every natural number $i$, let $s_i = \sum_{j=0}^{i-1} n_{k-j}$, where $n_j$ denotes the binary digit of $n$ at position $j$. Then the Takagi coefficient $\ell_{i+1}(n, k)$ equals $s_i$ if $n_{k-i} = 0$, and equals $i - s_i$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Formula for the Takagi coefficients

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $k$, the Takagi coefficient $\ell_0(n, k)$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The Takagi coefficient at index zero

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $k$ an integer, and write $n_j$ for the binary digit of $n$ at position $j$ (so $n_j = 0$ for $j < 0$). The Takagi coefficients $\ell_i(n, k)$, for natural numbers $i$, are the natural numbers given by $\ell_0(n, k) = 0$ and, for every natural number $i$, with $s_i = \sum_{j=0}^{i-1} n_{k-j}$, by $\ell_{i+1}(n, k) = s_i$ if $n_{k-i} = 0$ and $\ell_{i+1}(n, k) = i - s_i$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Takagi coefficients

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $k$, the Takagi value $\tau(n, k)$ of the dyadic presentation $n / 2^{k+1}$ satisfies $\tau(n, k) = \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} \ell_{i+1}(n, k) / 2^{i+1}$, where $\ell_i(n, k)$ denotes the $i$-th Takagi coefficient of $n$ and $k$.
nodes.title: Series for the Takagi value

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and an integer $k$, the Takagi value $\tau(n, k)$ of the dyadic presentation $n / 2^{k+1}$ is the sum of the real series $\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} \ell_{i+1}(n, k) / 2^{i+1}$, where $\ell_i(n, k)$ denotes the $i$-th Takagi coefficient of $n$ and $k$.
nodes.title: Takagi function on dyadic presentations

nodes.summary: Every divide-and-conquer tree with $n$ leaves has exactly $\delta(n)$ $D$-nodes, where $\delta$ is the function on positive integers given by $\delta(1) = 0$, $\delta(2m) = 2\delta(m)$ and $\delta(2m+1) = \delta(m) + \delta(m+1) + 1$ for $m \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Coronado et al.'s count of $D$-nodes in divide-and-conquer trees

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a full binary tree with $n$ leaves and let $a$ be the number of $S$-nodes of $t$. Then the number of $D$-nodes of $t$ is $n - 1 - a$ (subtraction of natural numbers, truncated at $0$).
nodes.title: $D$-nodes and $S$-nodes of a full binary tree

nodes.summary: Write $D(t)$ for the number of $D$-nodes of a full binary tree $t$. If the root of $t$ has left subtree $l$ and right subtree $r$, then $D(t) = \varepsilon + D(l) + D(r)$, where $\varepsilon = 0$ if $l$ and $r$ have the same number of leaves and $\varepsilon = 1$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Recursion for the number of $D$-nodes

nodes.summary: A $D$-node of a full binary tree is an interior node whose two subtrees have different numbers of leaves. The number of $D$-nodes of a full binary tree is the number of its interior nodes that are $D$-nodes.
nodes.title: Number of $D$-nodes of a full binary tree

nodes.summary: The full binary tree consisting of a single leaf has no $D$-nodes and no $S$-nodes, and it is a divide-and-conquer tree.
nodes.title: The single-leaf tree

nodes.summary: Write $S(t)$ for the number of $S$-nodes of a full binary tree $t$. If the root of $t$ has left subtree $l$ and right subtree $r$, then $S(t) = \varepsilon + S(l) + S(r)$, where $\varepsilon = 1$ if $l$ and $r$ have the same number of leaves and $\varepsilon = 0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Recursion for the number of $S$-nodes

nodes.summary: An $S$-node of a full binary tree is an interior node whose two subtrees have the same number of leaves. The number of $S$-nodes of a full binary tree is the number of its interior nodes that are $S$-nodes.
nodes.title: Number of $S$-nodes of a full binary tree

nodes.summary: For a natural number $i$, let $s_1(i)$ denote the sum of the binary digits of $i$. Then for every natural number $m$, $2 \sum_{i < 2^m} s_1(i) = 2^m m$; that is, the binary expansions of $0, 1, \dots, 2^m - 1$ contain $2^m m / 2$ ones in total.
nodes.title: Sum of binary digit sums below a power of two

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
